title: preflight-oncall-dropin-30min-scratch-tess
content:
Purpose
- 30-minute drop-in for the oncall rotation handoff this Friday 09:30 PT. Keep it tight: status, risks, one action each team. This is a prep scratchpad — not final wording.

Agenda (10–12 min speaking, rest Q&A)
1) Quick status snapshot (2–3 min)
   - Current global SLOs: token-latency 99p < 1800ms, availability 99.95% (see runbook metrics).
   - Active incidents: none open > Sev-2. Minor degradation detected yesterday for eu-west (transient spikes, resolved by autoscale).
2) Known risk windows (3 min)
   - Scheduled infra maintenance on Sat 02:00–04:00 PT (OPS-4123) — expect short cold-starts on Dedicated pools.
   - New model rollout (canary) for text-generation-v2 on Mon — watch memory pressure and tail latency.
3) Immediate asks (1–2 min)
   - Please validate the eviction thresholds in the eu-west A pool (ticket in linked artifacts).
   - If you see >5% error-rate regression in embeddings endpoint, escalate to SRE lead and attach traces.
4) Short scripts & Slack templates (1–2 min)
   - Paging script (callout): "Paging SRE-1: Observed sustained 5xx increase on hosted-api/embeddings — request immediate triage. Link: <ops runbook> OPS-4123."
   - User-facing short notice (if needed): "We're investigating higher-than-normal latency for embeddings in EU. No data loss expected. Updates at 1s/min."

Runbook pointers (one-liners for drop-in)
- Latency spike: follow /runbooks/latency-spike -> prefix cache check, mem-usage, kernel-fallback toggles.
- Autoscale flapping: check HPA logs, webhook latency, and recent config pushes in infra repo.
- Failover to cheaper region: pre-approved policy for critical customers — see console rollout -> failover checklist.

Practical notes to say out loud (tone: calm, operational)
- "We don't anticipate a user-facing outage; this is a precautionary handoff so everyone knows the risk windows and quick fixes."
- Keep comms short and factual. If a noisy incident happens, we will switch to bridge-mode and longer comms.

Anticipated Q&A + suggested answers
Q: "How bad were yesterday's eu-west spikes?"
A: "Transient — 95/99p both rose ~200–400ms for ~18 min around 11:20 PT. Autoscale caught up; no customer retries noted. I've attached sample traces to OPS-4123."
Q: "Do we need to pause the model rollout?"
A: "Not yet — canary passes basic health checks. We will hold the rollout if tail latency regresses by >20% or if memory swap begins across nodes. SRE can flip the hold flag in the deploy console."

Cheat-sheet for whoever's oncall next
- First 5 min: check /metrics/dashboards (latency, errors, queue-length), then glance at recent deploys.
- If 5xx > 1% sustained for 5 min -> open incident channel, tag SRE-1 and infra lead.
- If onboarding customers report errors, correlate keys to routes and look for token-usage anomalies.

Open items (todo)
- [ ] Summarize last week's capacity anomalies into a 1-paragraph note for Monday sync (assigned: Tess).
- [ ] Add a line in the shift handbook about 'canary pause criteria' (assigned: Aisha).
- [ ] Confirm weekend maintenance notice reachability (email + slack) — Rowan to confirm by Thu.

Notes to self (scratchy)
- Bring up 'kv-cache eviction threshold' in Friday eng-standup if not fixed.
- Consider small pre-warm for Dedicated pools during maintenance to avoid cold-starts (cost vs. latency trade-off).
- Double-check that the rollback playbook includes steps for model weights mismatch (we had a near-miss last month).

Potential comm phrasing for an urgent outage (short)
- "We are currently investigating increased errors on the Hosted API. Engineers are engaged and we will post updates every 10 minutes. No customer data loss expected at this time."

End of scratchpad — convert to final short-dropin agenda + two slide summary before Fri morning if we want a visual.

Latest refs:
- OPS-4123 (Jira): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4123
- Shift handbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/shift-handbook
- Slack: #oncall (pinned runbooks and incident templates)

---
